editorial:
Imagine a guy who is a total superstar on stage, covered in sequins and loved by millions, but is actually a monster behind closed doors. That is exactly what you get with this documentary. It takes you deep into the life of Gary Glitter, a man who used his fame and loud personality to hide the fact that he was hurting children. You will see old clips of his big hits and hear from people who knew him in the music world, but the real focus is on the victims and the lawyers who tried to put him away. It feels less like a music movie and more like a true crime investigation that shows how a predator can hide in plain sight for years.

What really hits hard is how the film shows Glitter slipping through the cracks of the legal system for so long. The pacing is steady, and the mix of archive footage and new interviews makes it feel very complete. It is a tough watch because the subject is so dark, but it is important to see how he manipulated everyone around him. If you enjoy deep dives into the dark side of fame, you should definitely check this out. Since it is available on ITVX, you can stream it easily, but if you want the best quality, look for a high-def version to see those old archives clearly.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing how Glitter finally ran out of places to hide. After years of moving between countries and dodging the law, he eventually faced the music in court. It explains that his fame didn't save him in the end, but it did let him get away with his crimes for way too long. The final scenes leave you thinking about how the system failed the victims for decades.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves true crime and exposes of famous people.
